newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Chip industry jitters hit Hyundai IPO subscription.
newsitem.headline: Chip industry jitters hit Hyundai IPO subscription.

text.p: The initial public offering (IPO) by Hyundai Electronics Industries Co attracted less attention than eight others that took place on November 19 and 20, Dongsuh Securities said on Thursday.

Hyundai Electronics, one of South Korea's three largest semiconductor makers and a unit of the giant Hyundai Group, offered 10 million shares for 20,000 won per share. The IPO was 5.08 times subscribed.
The eight other IPOs that took place during the same period were subscribed between 6.17 and 66.47 times.
Market analysts said the poor performance for Hyundai Electronics reflected continued concerns among investors about the sluggish global semiconductor industry.
Falling international prices of memory chips as a result of a persisting global oversupply have eroded profits of major chipmakers, they said.
The highest competition ratio of 66.47 times was set on Kukdong City Gas Co's offering of 1.8 million shares, Dongsuh said in a statement.
Samsung Engineering Co, Kuk Dong Corp, Sewon Chemical Co, Muhak Alcohol Co, Dong Nam Chemical Industries Co, Sindoricoh Co and Fursys Inc also offered their shares during the two days.
The nine companies are expected to list their shares on the Seoul stock market in January, according to Korea Stock Exchange officials.
